sourceRecords.text: Reclaim Your Investment. Surround yourself with FormerFeds who share your mission ™ File a Claim If you already signed up to be a client, click here. Notice: All Himalaya Exchange clients who intend to file a forfeiture remission petition must do so by October 22, 2025.We are preparing our final ancillary petition filings on October 21, 2025. We will seek to challenge the U.S. government’s jurisdiction to seize HEX funds, along with other claims. Once again, we will propose a secure and safe method by which the government can collaborate with HEX to authenticate your claims and facilitate the return of funds.If you are a client, please complete the enclosed affidavit here.We will also argue that by signing up with us for representation—even without a signed affidavit—that should suffice under these unique circumstances to perfect your claims.We cannot predict how the honorable court will rule. sourceRecords.title: Important Update on Himalaya Exchange Forfeiture Process
sourceRecords.text: Today, the U.S. government wisely filed a motion with the court to restart the forfeiture process following Miles Guo’s sentencing. This important move aligns with our consistent advocacy across three prior filings, aiming to expedite the fair return of funds seized from our 6,575 Himalaya Exchange (HEX) members. In the latest motion, we reiterate our demand for transparency, fairness, and due process in returning the illegally seized investment funds. Our request emphasizes the necessity for procedural safeguards and seeks restitution under a constructive trust, clearly demonstrating that the seized assets belong rightfully to HEX members. We continue to advocate vigorously for the rights of all HEX members, demanding not only the return of seized assets but also accrued interest, administrative expenses, and attorneys’ fees. Justice requires swift action, and today’s motion is a welcomed step toward achieving restitution for all affected investors. Stay informed here for continuous updates and next steps. sourceRecords.text: 紧急：没收阶段与申索提交流程 定罪后申索流程 & 处理费用 我们承诺在整个没收过程中代表您，但须经法院批准。下方提供了必须签署的宣誓书链接，以继续您的申索。 我们将代表您提出有力的法律论据；但请注意，结果无法保证，最终裁决由法院决定。 请保持关注，并在此页面查看最新更新。 鉴于法院裁决的不确定性，我们强烈建议您收集您的账户信息作为预防措施。HEX 将与我们一起积极参与此过程。 定罪后的没收程序是新引入的法律阶段，比之前的诉讼程序复杂得多。不同于早期阶段由政府承担举证责任，现在申索人必须主动证明其合法所有权，提供详细的财务文件，并确立其申索的确切金额。 政府基于未经证实的指控查封资产，往往没有明确的理由。为了有效反击，我们将整理和处理大量申索人名单、法律文件和财务记录，以证实这些资金应属于 HEX 成员。此外，我们正在倡导前所未有的数据安全保护措施。 我们已核对客户名单，目前正在接受新的申索人。如需加入此法律行动，您必须填写并签署以下链接中的表格。 为了推进这一复杂的法律行动，需预先支付 $25 – $50 的处理费用（根据您的经济能力），适用于所有寻求代理并希望加入团体申索的申索人。这笔资金将帮助我们建立坚实的法律基础，以对抗没收程序。如果大多数申索人提供支持，我们将拥有必要的资源来应对政府异议，并最大程度地提高追回被没收资产的可能性。 我们的法律策略包括提交合并的法律申索，并向法院请求接受统一的附属申诉。我们的法律团队已确定，每位申索人都必须单独提交声明，以符合这两个法律程序的要求。 及时支付处理费用至关重要——该程序极为耗时，我们的团队需要日夜工作，以满足关键期限。美国政府已将该程序设计得极具挑战性，尤其是在当前情况下。您的参与和支持对于这场正义斗争至关重要。 在填写以下宣誓书之前，请确保您已完成 注册协议。 支票邮寄地址： PO Box 3070 Cinnaminson, NJ 08077​ ​ ​ 银行电汇： 美国银行（Bank of America） 汇款路径（Routing）： 026009593 账户号码（Account）： 381046237789 Venmo： @bee-guyer Stripe： https://buy.stripe.com/7sI29O2Lt2QCa8UeUV GiveSendGo：​ ​GiveSendGo | 刑事没收阶段

sourceRecords.text: Urgent: Forfeiture Stage & Claim Filing Process POST-CONVICTION CLAIM PROCESS & PROCESSING FEE We are committed to representing you throughout the forfeiture process, subject to court approval. Below, you will find a link to an affidavit that must be signed to proceed with your claim. We will put forth strong legal arguments on your behalf; however, please be advised that there are no guarantees, and all outcomes are ultimately subject to court determination. Stay informed and monitor this page for updates. Given the uncertainty surrounding how the court will rule, we strongly recommend gathering your account information as a precautionary measure. HEX will be actively involved in this process alongside us. The post-conviction forfeiture process is a newly introduced and significantly more complex legal stage compared to earlier proceedings. Unlike prior stages where the government bore the burden of proof, claimants must now actively demonstrate their rightful ownership, provide detailed financial documentation, and establish the exact monetary value of their claim. The government has seized assets based on unproven allegations, often without clear justification. To effectively challenge this, we will be compiling and processing extensive claimant lists, legal documentation, and financial records to substantiate that these funds rightfully belong to HEX members. Additionally, we are advocating for unprecedented data security protections. We have reconciled our client list and are currently accepting new claimants. To be included in this legal effort, you must complete and sign the form linked below. To facilitate this complex legal endeavor, a processing fee of $25 – $50 (based on your financial capability) is required in advance from each claimant seeking representation and inclusion in the group filings. This contribution will enable us to build a strong legal foundation to contest the forfeiture proceedings. If most claimants contribute, we will have the necessary resources to address government objections and maximize the chances of reclaiming seized assets. Our legal strategy involves filing consolidated legal claims and petitioning the court to accept a unified ancillary petition. Our legal team has determined that each claimant must individually file a statement to satisfy both legal processes. Timely payment of the processing fee is crucial—this is a highly time-intensive process, requiring our team to work around the clock to meet critical deadlines. The U.S. government has designed this process to be extremely challenging to navigate, particularly under these circumstances. Your participation and support are essential in this fight for justice. Before completing the affidavit below, please ensure you have already completed the Signup agreement. sourceRecords.title: Important Update on Himalaya Exchange Forfeiture Process
sourceRecords.text: Important Update on Himalaya Exchange Forfeiture Process Today, the U.S. government wisely filed a motion with the court to restart the forfeiture process following Miles Guo’s sentencing. This important move aligns with our consistent advocacy across three prior filings, aiming to expedite the fair return of funds seized from our 6,575 Himalaya Exchange (HEX) members. In the latest motion, we reiterate our demand for transparency, fairness, and due process in returning the illegally seized investment funds. Our request emphasizes the necessity for procedural safeguards and seeks restitution under a constructive trust, clearly demonstrating that the seized assets belong rightfully to HEX members. We continue to advocate vigorously for the rights of all HEX members, demanding not only the return of seized assets but also accrued interest, administrative expenses, and attorneys’ fees. Justice requires swift action, and today’s motion is a welcomed step toward achieving restitution for all affected investors. Stay informed here for continuous updates and next steps.

sourceRecords.title: March 22, 2025: BREAKING UPDATE: FormerFedsGroup Takes Bold Action to Protect Thousands of HEX Victims
sourceRecords.text: March 22, 2025: BREAKING UPDATE: FormerFedsGroup Takes Bold Action to Protect Thousands of HEX Victims In a powerful legal filing submitted to the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, the FormerFedsGroup.Com through attorney Bradford L. Geyer, is advocating fiercely on behalf of over 5,200 innocent members of the Himalaya Exchange (HEX) whose funds were unjustly caught in government forfeiture actions. The recent filing highlights serious procedural irregularities, emphasizing the government’s inadequate notification methods, rushed forfeiture processes, and potential violations of fundamental due process rights. FormerFedsGroup is urging the Court to: Vacate the government’s preliminary forfeiture order until proper procedures are established. Suspend current deadlines that force victims into hasty and potentially harmful filings. Ensure a secure, transparent, and humanitarian approach to returning seized assets to victims, safeguarding their identities, and protecting them from retaliation or exploitation. Attorney Bradford L. Geyer argues persuasively that the government’s actions prematurely deprived HEX members of their due process rights by imposing unreasonable deadlines and inadequate notification methods. The filing underscores the need for judicial oversight to prevent further irreparable harm and ensure compliance with the Crime Victims’ Rights Act, ultimately aiming to restore public trust and integrity. FormerFedsGroup remains committed to defending the rights of thousands of victims affected by government actions, ensuring justice, fairness, and transparency prevail. Stay tuned for further developments as FormerFedsGroup continues its steadfast advocacy on behalf of these innocent HEX members. If you are a HEX customer and wish to be represented, you can find the sign up here. sourceRecords.title: A Call for Justice: Motions Filed to Restore Seized Funds to Himalaya Exchange Investors
sourceRecords.text: A Call for Justice: Motions Filed to Restore Seized Funds to Himalaya Exchange Investors Motion Filed to Return Funds to Himalaya Exchange Victims Attorney Bradford L. Geyer has filed a critical motion on behalf of over 6,500 victims demanding the return of funds seized by the U.S. Government from Himalaya Exchange depositors. The motion argues that these individuals—many of whom face serious risks—are legally entitled to restitution under federal law, including 18 U.S.C. § 3771. The filings expose a lack of transparency, risks of forced public disclosure, and inconsistent instructions from the DOJ. They propose an organized, privacy-respecting process for submitting claims, backed by secure data from the Himalaya Exchange’s internal records. The government has already acknowledged its intent to return assets, but without a clear path. These motions aim to fix that and ensure victims are treated justly—not punished further. files.title: ORDER granting 1 Motion for Discovery. Petitioner Rui Hao petitions this Court for an order, pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1782, authorizing it to take the testimony of Ho Wan Kwok a/k/a Miles Guo ("Kwok"), Reg. No. 49134-510, who is curre ntly held at the Metropolitan Detention Center ("MDC Brooklyn"). That motion is granted. The Court finds that (1) Kwok resides or is found in this District, (2) the discovery is for use in a foreign proceeding before a foreign tribunal, and (3) the application for discovery is made by an interested person. See Brandi-Dohrn v. IKB Deutsche Industriebank AG, 673 F.3d 76, 80 (2d Cir. 2012). Having also balanced the factors set forth in Intel Corp. v. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. , 542 U.S. 241, 26465 (2004), the Court grants Hao's petition.Accordingly, Petitioner is granted leave to take the testimony of Kwok via videoconference on July 22 and 23, 2026 for trial in the British Virgin Islands. MDC Brooklyn and the Federal Bureau of Prisons are directed to produce Ho Wan Kwok, Reg. No. 49134-510, for his testimony by videoconference on July 22 and 23, 2026, and to coordinate his appearance with Petitioner's counsel. Ordered by Magistrate Judge Clay H. Kaminsky on 7/9/2026.
